idiom_name: struct + per-row CRUD functions over the SQLite C API
implementation_notes: C has no ORM, so the classic structure is reproduced literally: a struct holds the columns, and free functions named after it (person_save, person_load, person_delete) are the record's methods. The mechanical steps are prepare-compile (sqlite3_prepare_v2), value binding (sqlite3_bind_*), execution (sqlite3_step) and teardown (sqlite3_finalize), with the primary key deciding INSERT versus UPDATE. What replaces the language's missing member functions is a naming convention plus a function-pointer table when polymorphic handlers are needed; the classic hand-written form stays justified for small embedded schemas, but once several tables interact the same functions become a hand-rolled data mapper.
pitfalls: Bind lifetimes: SQLITE_STATIC keeps a pointer to the caller's buffer, so a temporary (stack) string must use SQLITE_TRANSIENT or be finalised before the buffer dies.
Every early return must still reach sqlite3_finalize; a leaked statement also keeps the database locked and the row-object code hides that leak well.
No transactions are implied: several person_save calls can leave a half-updated graph unless they run inside BEGIN/COMMIT.
